results: 1. smooth pursuit and saccades: ocular motor apraxia - failure to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades with compensatory head thrusts
2. facial dysmorphism and general examination: facial dysmorphism in all patients - broad nasal bridge and low-set ears most common
3. genetic testing (exome): pathogenic variants in ciliopathy genes on exome sequencing
4. MRI brain with DWI: MOLAR TOOTH SIGN with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and horizontally aligned superior cerebellar peduncles
dx_raw:
Based on the clinical presentation (ocular motor apraxia, feeding difficulties, visual impairment) and the definitive investigation findings—specifically the **molar tooth sign** on MRI (pathognomonic) and the presence of pathogenic variants in **ciliopathy genes**—the diagnosis is clear.

DIAGNOSIS: Joubert syndrome (an autosomal recessive ciliopathy caused by mutations in genes encoding primary cilia components).

Alternatives:
1. Dandy-Walker malformation
2. Pontine Tegmental Cap Dysplasia
3. Isolated cerebellar hypoplasia
dx: Joubert syndrome (an autosomal recessive ciliopathy caused by mutations in genes encoding primary cilia components).
